skill.name: complexity-analyzer
skill.description: Measure and report code complexity metrics with actionable recommendations.
skill.summary: Measure and report code complexity metrics with actionable recommendations.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

content.value_statement: Complex code is hard to review, test, and maintain. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code measure complexity metrics and produce focused refactoring guidance.
actual_capabilities: Measures cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, Halstead metrics, nesting depth, and lines of code.
Reports function-level metrics such as parameters, return points, length, and complexity rating.
Summarizes file and module complexity with averages, hotspots, and duplicate code indicators.
Ranks the most complex functions and groups results by complexity threshold.
Provides refactoring recommendations for long functions, deep nesting, and excessive parameters.
References common language tools for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, and Ruby.
limitations: Exact metric calculation depends on access to the relevant source files.
Some language-specific metrics may require external analysis tools to be installed.
The skill recommends refactoring steps but does not automatically rewrite code.
Complexity scores should be reviewed with test coverage and business context.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Identify the highest complexity functions before a cleanup sprint.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Request Risk
use_cases.description: Check whether changed files add complex control flow or long functions.

use_cases.title: Track Maintainability Trends
use_cases.description: Compare complexity scores across modules to guide maintenance planning.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use complexity-analyzer on this file. Report the main complexity scores, the most complex functions, and the top refactoring recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Scan A Source Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use complexity-analyzer on src/. Summarize average complexity, list the ten highest-risk functions, and group recommendations by priority.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Before And After
prompt_templates.prompt: Use complexity-analyzer to compare this branch with the previous version. Show which functions improved, worsened, or still exceed the target threshold.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Refactoring Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use complexity-analyzer across the project. Create a refactoring roadmap based on cyclomatic complexity, nesting depth, function length, and maintainability impact.

output_examples.input: Analyze a payment module with several long functions.
output_examples.output: The report highlights processPayment as high complexity, explains the main branch and nesting issues, and recommends extracting validation, fee calculation, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes service logic.
output_examples.output: The review notes that average complexity stayed stable, but one new function exceeds the target threshold and needs more focused tests.

output_examples.input: Assess a full source directory before planning maintenance work.
output_examples.output: The summary ranks the most complex modules, separates urgent refactoring from monitoring items, and suggests practical next steps for each hotspot.

best_practices: Run the skill on focused directories so findings stay actionable.
Review high complexity results with recent change history and defect data.
Use the recommendations to split large refactors into small reviewable changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a single complexity score as proof that code is incorrect.
Do not refactor stable business logic without tests or product context.
Do not ignore moderate complexity that changes often or lacks coverage.

faq.question: Which complexity metrics does this skill discuss?
faq.answer: It covers cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, Halstead metrics, maintainability index, nesting depth, and lines of code.

faq.question: Can it analyze an entire project?
faq.answer: Yes, it can summarize project-level complexity when the relevant files are available in the workspace.

faq.question: Does it make code changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis and recommendations, while the user decides which refactors to apply.

faq.question: Can it compare complexity across versions?
faq.answer: Yes, it can compare available before-and-after code and explain where complexity changed.

faq.question: Does it require a specific programming language?
faq.answer: No. The guidance covers several common languages, but exact metrics may depend on available language tools.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Use the results to prioritize risky hotspots, plan tests, and choose smaller refactoring steps.
